pr_title: core: support top level drop-ins through -.service.d for service units
pr_body:
This change will support adding overrides in `-.service.d` that will modify unit settings for all service units. I've opted only for service units at this time since:

- the use of `-.<unit type>` is currently different between types (i.e. slice and mount) so this feature probably shouldn't be expanded to units already using `-.<unit type>`.
- there is a use case for services to have this, but it's not clear there is a use case for other unit types.

In addition to the drop-in behavior, this change will also blacklist using `-.service` and variants (i.e. `-@.service`) from being a usable as unit names, as that would cause too much confusion when doing overrides the one service (-.service) vs. multiple services.

Closes #12830
pr_comments:
Hmm, this is interesting. Right now we have two approaches:

1. The new DefaultXXX settings which are hierarchy specific and generic across units (eg. DefaultMemoryLow)
2. The older DefaultXXX settings which are propagated globally by the manager (eg. DefaultTasksMax)

What kind of things are you thinking about having be globally service-specific instead of hierarchy-specific (ie. couldn't be implemented via option 1)? I'm not against this change in principle, but just want to make sure we don't present too many options for doing similar things if they can be amalgamated.

@cdown  We're looking to run a binary checker on services before they start and gate the start up of a service based on the age of the binaries in the unit. AFAICT, the DefaultXYZ= configurations are not suited for running arbitrary binaries (i.e. it lacks the settings that service unit properties provide for exec-ing).

hmm, i am not sure i like the semantics of this, given that this is not extensible to .mount or slice units, since there -.slice and -.mount have a different meaning, and thus you couldn't do drop-ins there which apply to all units of this type.

Can't we find a better naming for this?

maybe say that doesn't mix "drop-in for everything" and "drop-in for the 'root' object of some kind"?

one idea: "--.service.d/"? or maybe just "service.d/"?
(also, I don't like that service_unit_name_is_valid() eats up OOM errors silently, returning an incorrect value in that case)

> hmm, i am not sure i like the semantics of this, given that this is not extensible to .mount or slice units, since there -.slice and -.mount have a different meaning, and thus you couldn't do drop-ins there which apply to all units of this type.

Huh, that's true. The `service.d` naming sounds reasonable to me at least.

> also, I don't like that service_unit_name_is_valid() eats up OOM errors silently, returning an incorrect value in that case

Originally this was `assert_se`, which I suggested was unwise since it means that might trigger just due to low memory situations. How changing it to return an int and returning `log_oom()`?

> one idea: "--.service.d/"? or maybe just "service.d/"?

`service.d/` also sounds good to me. `--.service.d/` is a bit excessive on hyphens.

I'll put up another PR to change the path and address the OOM checks. Though if the special name is changed to `service.d/` that whole helper function might not even be needed anymore.

issue_context.title: running system-wide checks on ExecStart= binary paths
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I'd like to run a binary checker of sorts on all the systemd services on a system. The arguments to the checker should be the binary paths specified in `ExecStart=` (optionally, all the binaries for every `ExecXYZ=` field in a service).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I think combined with `ExecCondition=` for services at https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/10596, I would need a way to make this a systemd-wide override (drop-in?) and also a special keyword (like the unit specifiers) to generically refer to the binary paths.

Would appreciate feedback on this proposal.
comments: I proposed in #11936 to extend `systemctl list-units` tool to analyze all units on the system. Perhaps this would also be useful in your case?

when do you want to run this? right before a service is started? or offline, after the system is up?

what's the precise usecase? i.e. what do you want to do in those checkers?

@poettering Right before the service starts (why I think ExecCondition= might be useful for this).

Our end use case is to check if binary has a certain header and when it was last built in order to prevent service start up if it's too old. But the framework could have more generally applicable uses like checking signatures on ELF binaries or other validity checks.
i see. ExecCondition could work for that I presume?
(i.e. as discussed in that other bug)

Yup ExecCondition= will work. But I'm not clear on the best way to generically apply this system-wide. I would like to avoid modifying/querying every service's unit individually by laying down one config somewhere (AFAIK this isn't possible).

In my head the config might look something like:
```
/etc/systemd/system/-.service.d/checker.conf:
  [Service]
  ExecCondition=/path/to/bin_checker %symbol that will pass in ExecStart= paths%
```

hmm, yeah we could probably extend the prefix drop-in logic so that a top-level dropin like you are suggesting is also honoured. But we should probably add a big big warning to the docs, that using this too much is a bad idea, except if you really know what you are doing.

review_comments: Huh! I guess that was an oversight, thanks.
